titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 10/2011 (މުދަލާއި ޚިދުމަތުގެ އަގުން ޓެކްސް ނެގުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Goods and Services Tax Act (Law No. 10/2011). It changes one GST rate set in Article 15(a). The current 16% rate in paragraph (5), which runs from 1 January 2023, would be given an end date in 2025. A new paragraph (6) would set the rate at 17% from a date in 2025 (the month is hard to read on the scan). The Majlis debate record describes this as the tourism GST.
whyItMatters: The affected GST rate would go up by one percentage point, from 16% to 17%, so goods and services taxed at that rate would cost slightly more from 2025.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 replaces Article 15(a)(5) so that the 16% rate applies from 1 January 2023 only up to a fixed date in 2025 (the printed day is 31, month hard to read).
Clause 2 adds a new Article 15(a)(6): 17% from a date in 2025 onward (month hard to read).
Clause 3 deals with when the Act takes effect, after ratification and publication in the Government Gazette. A 30-day period is mentioned, but its exact effect could not be read reliably.
Clause 4 is a short interpretation clause saying what 'the Act' means in this bill.
The financial note says the bill lists estimated extra income of MVR 201.9 million in 2025, MVR 330.8 million in 2026 and MVR 538.4 million in 2027.
whoIsAffected: Businesses charging this GST rate and the people who buy from them.
statedReasons: The explanatory note is too hard to read in full. The financial note estimates extra income of MVR 201.9 million in 2025.
